mainTopic: Cooking meat on שבת (מאכל בן דרוסאי) and the איסור of making a מנחה חמץ
overview: The amud opens with רבי יוחנן's ruling that someone who puts meat on coals on שבת is חייב only if he turns it over. The גמרא first uses this ruling to challenge an earlier rule about leavening a מנחה, and רבא answers that leavening counts like a full act of roasting. The גמרא then asks what case רבי יוחנן means, and answers that one side cooked only to the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי counts as nothing, while both sides at that level counts as cooking. רבא adds that a גרוגרת-sized area roasted on one side makes one חייב. There are two versions of whether that area must be in one spot or can be spread out, and the משנה about drilling a tiny hole is tested against each version. Next, a ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the איסור of making a מנחה חמץ covers the whole מנחה and every kind of מנחה, but only a fit one. רב פפא and רב מרי each ask about an edge case of this איסור, and both questions end in תיקו. Finally, the גמרא asks what the words 'אשר תקריבו' add. רבי יוסי הגלילי says they include מנחת נסכים, and רבי עקיבא says they include לחם הפנים. The גמרא then begins to challenge רבי יוסי הגלילי, since מנחת נסכים is made with oil, which counts as fruit juice. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Meat on coals: turning it over decides liability
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that someone who puts meat on coals on שבת is חייב only if he turns it over. The גמרא uses this to challenge the earlier ruling about leaven on מנחה dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If someone placed meat on coals, he is liable if he turned it over, and exempt if he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן's ruling about meat on coals on שבת. It brings it as a challenge to the earlier ruling that putting leaven on מנחה dough makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, simply placing the meat is not enough for liability; turning it over is what makes it count. If so, putting leaven on dough without turning the dough should also not make a person liable. That seems to clash with the earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He placed or put down
Burning coals
He turned it over
Liable, deserving punishment
Exempt, not liable

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
if one placed meat on top of coals,
if he turned it over, he is liable;
if he did not turn it over, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הִנִּיחַ בָּשָׂר עַל גַּבֵּי גֶּחָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought as a challenge to the earlier ruling about leaven on מנחה dough
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ruling that putting leaven on מנחה dough makes a person liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If meat needs to be turned over before there is liability, leaven placed on dough without turning should also not create liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat on coals on שבת: turned over means חייב, not turned over means פטור.

steps.title: רבא: the leaven case is like the full roasting act
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'liable' in the leaven case means it is like the completed roasting act of שבת, the one where the meat was turned over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'liable' also mean there? It means like the act of roasting on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He explains that the 'liable' ruling about leaven means the act is like a complete roasting on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting leaven on the dough is treated like the meat that was turned over, which is the case where there is liability. So there is no clash with רבי יוחנן. The leaven act counts as the full act, even without turning the dough.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasting
The act of, the doing of
What does he mean when he says

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the meaning of 'liable' that was also said?
phrases.notes: This 'liable' is the earlier ruling about leaven on the מנחה dough, not the meat case.

phrases.english: Like the act of roasting on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי ״חַיָּיב״ נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaven on dough without turning would be like meat not turned over, so it should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaven on dough is like the full roasting act, the turned-over case, so it is liable.

steps.title: Returning to רבי יוחנן's ruling itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now studies רבי יוחנן's ruling on its own, quoting it again through רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone placed meat on coals, he is liable if he turned it over, and exempt if he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to examine רבי יוחנן's ruling directly. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ruling was only a tool for challenging the leaven case. Now the ruling itself becomes the subject. The גמרא repeats it in full, this time naming רבה בר בר חנה as the one who reported it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to study a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
if one placed meat on top of coals,
if he turned it over, he is liable;
if he did not turn it over, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 1 in order to analyze it on its own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat on coals: turned over means חייב, not turned over means פטור.

steps.title: What case is this? Either obvious or hard to understand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי יוחנן means. If the meat would not cook without turning, the ruling is obvious. If it would cook anyway, why is he exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say that without turning it would not cook, that is obvious! But if it would cook even without turning, why is he not liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to picture the case and finds a problem with both options. Either the ruling teaches nothing new, or it seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the meat would not cook unless turned. Then of course he is exempt without turning, so why say it? Option two: the meat would cook anyway. Then placing it alone should already make him liable, so the exemption makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
If you say (first possible option)
It is obvious, so why say it?
Why?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say that if he did not turn it over
it would not cook, that is obvious!
Rather, it is where even if he does not turn it over
it would still cook;
then why is he not liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּאִי לָא הִיפֵּךְ בֵּיהּ לָא בְּשִׁיל – פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind the ruling just restated
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that he is exempt if he did not turn the meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every way of picturing the case fails: either the ruling is obvious, or the exemption seems wrong.

steps.title: One side at the בן דרוסאי level counts as nothing
steps.stepSummary: The case is where one side alone reaches only the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי, and turning it over brings both sides to that level. רבי יוחנן teaches that one side alone counts as nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where, without turning, it would cook on one side to the level of בן דרוסאי's food, and when he turns it, it cooks on both sides to that level. This teaches us that anything cooked on only one side to the level of בן דרוסאי's food counts as nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a middle case. The meat does get somewhat cooked without turning, but only on one side, and that does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is neither of the two options from the question. Without turning, the meat is cooked a little, so the ruling is not obvious. Yet one side at the בן דרוסאי level is legally nothing; only both sides at that level counts as cooking, so turning creates the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case (introduces the specific case)
Food cooked only partly, the minimum level of cooking (like the food of בן דרוסאי)
On one side
This teaches us (the new point)
It is nothing, it does not count legally

steps.whatToRemember: Meat cooked on one side to the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי is not considered cooked for שבת. Once both sides reach that level, it counts as cooking and one is חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say that the meat stays raw without turning. It does get partly cooked on one side, but the הלכה treats that as nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the minimum standard of cooking for שבת liability: both sides must reach the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where if he did not turn it over,
it would cook on one side
like the food of ben Derosai,
phrases.notes: בן דרוסאי ate his food only partly cooked, so this phrase means the lowest level that counts as cooked.

phrases.english: and when he turns it over,
it cooks on both sides
like the food of ben Derosai,
and he teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל מִצַּד אֶחָד כְּמַאֲכָל בֶּן דְּרוֹסַאי –
phrases.english: that anything cooked on one side like the food of ben Derosai
is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי לָא הַפֵּיךְ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what case is this' challenge by finding a middle case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a specific middle case that is neither obvious nor contradictory
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the meat would not cook at all without turning (obvious), or it would fully cook (should be liable).
steps.terutzMaskana: One side at the בן דרוסאי level counts as nothing; both sides at that level is cooking, so turning makes him liable.

steps.title: A fig-sized roasted spot on one side makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a גרוגרת-sized piece of the meat was roasted on one side, in one spot, the person is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If an amount the size of a dried fig got roasted on one side, all in one spot, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule to רבי יוחנן's teaching. Even without turning the meat, a fig-sized area that got properly roasted on one side is enough for חיוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 we learned that one side cooked only to the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי counts as nothing. רבא says that if a real שיעור, a גרוגרת, got properly roasted, that is already a complete act of cooking. He adds the detail 'in one spot', and the next step questions it.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a dried fig, the standard שיעור for many שבת prohibitions
Was roasted
Liable, here for cooking on שבת

phrases.english: Rava said:
And if a fig-bulk of it was roasted
on one side, in one spot, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְאִם נִצְלָה בּוֹ כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where one side alone does count: a full גרוגרת roasted in one spot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גרוגרת-sized area roasted on one side, in one spot, makes one חייב.

steps.title: Challenge from the drilling case: small spots should join
steps.stepSummary: רבינא infers from רבא that two or three spots would not count. He challenges this from the משנה that one who drills even a tiny hole is חייב, which he reads as small holes that can join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב אשי: So in one spot, yes, but in two or three spots, no? But the משנה says one who drills any amount is liable! What is the case? If it is one spot, what use is a tiny hole? It must mean two or three spots, which can be joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא reads into רבא's words that scattered spots don't count. He attacks this using a משנה about drilling holes on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single tiny hole seems useless, so why would the משנה make one חייב for it? רבינא concludes that the משנה must mean several small holes that will later be joined into one big hole. If small separate holes add up for drilling, small separate roasted spots should add up for cooking too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who drills (a hole)
Any amount at all, even the tiniest
What is the case? How do we picture it?
Rather, is it not that...? (pushes toward a reading)
Joining together into one amount

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
In one spot, yes,
but in two or three spots, no?
But we learned: One who drills any amount is liable!
What is the case?
If you say in one spot,
what is a tiny hole fit for?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּשְׁנַיִם אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not in two or three spots,
which are fit to be joined together?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: הַקּוֹדֵחַ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'one spot' limit in רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from רבא that a גרוגרת spread over two or three spots does not make one חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה of drilling must mean several small holes that join together. So separate spots should also join in roasting.

steps.title: A single tiny hole is useful as a keyhole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of one tiny hole, which is useful as an opening for a key.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is one spot, because even a tiny hole is useful as an opening for a key.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבינא's reading of the משנה. A single tiny hole does have a use, so there is no proof that small spots join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's whole proof rested on the idea that one tiny hole is useless. Once we see it can serve as a keyhole, the משנה can be about one spot. So רבא's 'one spot' limit stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps the original reading)
An opening or doorway
A key

phrases.english: No, actually it is in one spot,
since it is fit as an opening for a key.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, דַּחֲזוּ לְבָבָא דְּאַקְלִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source: the משנה is about one useful tiny hole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single tiny hole is useless, so the משנה must mean joined holes.
steps.terutzMaskana: One tiny hole is useful as a keyhole, so the משנה proves nothing about joining spots.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבא counts only one spot, and the drilling משנה does not disprove it because one tiny hole can be a keyhole.

steps.title: Second version: even two or three spots count
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא rules that the גרוגרת counts even when it is spread over two or three spots.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: Even in two or three spots, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a second version of רבא's ruling. In this version separate roasted spots do add up to a גרוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version is the opposite of the first one. Here the small roasted areas join together, which is exactly the idea רבינא suggested in step 7. So in this version the drilling משנה could be a support, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, רבא counts only one spot. In the second, two or three spots also count.

phrases.english: And some say, Rava said:
Even in two or three spots.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבא's ruling from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גרוגרת roasted on one side counts even when spread over two or three spots.

steps.title: Trying to support the second version from the drilling case
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tries to prove the second version from the משנה of drilling. A tiny single hole seems useless, so the משנה must mean several holes that join.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: We also learned this: one who drills any amount is liable. What is the case? If one spot, what use is a tiny hole? It must mean two or three spots, which can be joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The same argument from step 7 now works as a proof. It supports רבא's second version instead of challenging it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning has not changed: a single tiny hole seems useless, so the משנה must mean small holes that join. What changed is how it is used. Here it backs up the idea that scattered roasted spots join together.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this: introduces support from a משנה
What is it fit for? What use does it have?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
We too have learned this:
One who drills any amount is liable.
What is the case?
If you say in one spot,
what is a tiny hole fit for?
Rather, is it not in two or three spots,
which are fit to be joined together?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא – הַקּוֹדֵחַ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the second version of רבא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's second version: two or three roasted spots join to make a גרוגרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'הקודח כל שהוא חייב', read as several small holes that can be joined.

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: one hole can be a keyhole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה can speak of one tiny hole, which is useful as a keyhole.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is one spot, because even a tiny hole is useful as an opening for a key.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off רבינא's proof with the same answer as before. The משנה does not have to be about holes joining together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one tiny hole is useful as a keyhole, the משנה can be about a single spot. So it gives no support to the idea of joining spots. רבא's second version still stands, but it has no proof from this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is fit (for use)
In one spot

steps.whatToRemember: The drilling משנה proves nothing either way. One tiny hole can serve as a keyhole, so it does not show that separate spots join.

phrases.english: No, actually it is in one spot,
since it is fit as an opening for a key.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, דַּחֲזוּ לְבָבָא דְּאַקְלִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבא's second version itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed one tiny hole is useless, but it can serve as a keyhole.

steps.title: A ברייתא on why the פסוק says 'מנחה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins explaining the פסוק of חמץ in a מנחה. Without the word 'מנחה', we would think only the קומץ is forbidden to be made חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If the verse had said only 'that you bring to ה׳ shall not be made leavened', I would say the prohibition covers only the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of making a מנחה חמץ. It opens a ברייתא that explains the words of the פסוק, and this is the setup for the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first shows what we would think if the פסוק lacked the word 'מנחה'. Only the קומץ goes on the מזבח, so we might limit the איסור to the קומץ alone. The next lines will show how the word 'מנחה' widens it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall not be made leavened: the איסור of making a מנחה חמץ
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
I have only...: the limited reading we would have had
You shall bring (as an offering)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If it had said only
"that you shall bring to the Lord shall not be made leavened,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11. The real פסוק also has the word מנחה, and the ברייתא asks what it adds.

phrases.english: I would say: I have only

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֹא תֵעָשֶׂה חָמֵץ אֶלָּא קוֹמֶץ בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: the handful alone included in "shall not be made leavened."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר ״אֲשֶׁר תַּקְרִיבוּ לַה׳ לֹא תֵעָשֶׂה חָמֵץ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of roasting on שבת and returns to the איסור of חמץ in a מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the word 'מנחה', the איסור of לא תעשה חמץ would cover only the קומץ.

steps.title: The whole meal offering and all kinds of meal offerings are included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'מנחה' that the whole מנחה, not only the קומץ, may not be made חמץ. From 'כל המנחה' it learns that every type of מנחה is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the whole מנחה is included? Because the פסוק says 'מנחה'. How do we know the other kinds of מנחות are included? Because the פסוק says 'כל המנחה' — every מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 12. It shows which word in the פסוק teaches each part of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we saw that without the word 'מנחה' we might think only the קומץ is forbidden to become חמץ. Now the ברייתא says the word 'מנחה' adds the whole מנחה, even before the קומץ is taken. The extra word 'כל' (all) then stretches the rule past the one kind of מנחה the פסוק is talking about, to every kind.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for the source in the פסוק)
The פסוק says (this is the source)
The other kinds of meal offerings
All; an extra word that includes more cases

phrases.english: From where do we know about the whole meal offering?
The verse says: "Meal offering."
From where do we know about the other meal offerings?
The verse says: "Every meal offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִנְחָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 12, giving the source that includes the whole מנחה and then all מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition of חמץ applies to the entire מנחה, even before the קומץ is taken, and to every type of מנחה.

steps.title: Only a fit meal offering is covered
steps.stepSummary: From 'אשר תקריבו לה׳' the ברייתא learns that the prohibition applies only to a כשרה מנחה. Leavening a fit one makes a person liable; leavening a disqualified one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That you shall bring to ה׳' means a fit מנחה, not a disqualified one. So the חכמים said: one who leavens a fit מנחה is liable, and one who leavens a disqualified מנחה is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now uses the next words of the פסוק to limit the rule. Only a מנחה that could really be brought to ה׳ is covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps so far widened the rule. Now these words narrow it. A מנחה that is already פסולה can no longer be 'brought to ה׳', so leavening it brings no punishment. This sets up רב פפא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, valid for offering
Disqualified, no longer valid for offering
One who makes it חמץ (leavens it)
Liable to punishment
Exempt from punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition against leavening a מנחה applies only to a fit מנחה. Leavening a disqualified one brings no liability.
steps.whyThisMatters: This exemption is the basis for רב פפא's question. If the מנחה becomes פסולה after the first leavening, does the exemption kick in?

phrases.english: "That you shall bring to the Lord" —
a fit one, and not a disqualified one.
From here they said:
One who leavens a fit one is liable,
and one who leavens a disqualified one is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֲשֶׁר תַּקְרִיבוּ לַה׳״ – כְּשֵׁרָה, וְלֹא פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, now limiting the prohibition to a fit מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leavening a fit מנחה makes one liable; leavening a disqualified מנחה does not.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about leavening again after it left the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about a מנחה that was leavened, then left the עזרה, and then was leavened again. Is the second leavening punishable?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: someone leavened the מנחה, then it went out of the עזרה, and then he leavened it again. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a question that mixes two rules. The next two steps lay out the two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first leavening was done on a fit מנחה, so he is surely liable for it. Then the מנחה left the עזרה, which normally makes it פסולה. The question is whether that later disqualification exempts the second leavening.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he was unsure about)
He leavened it
And it went out (left the עזרה)
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he leavened it, and it went out,
phrases.notes: It went out of the עזרה, the area where it is allowed to be.

phrases.english: and he then leavened it again — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: חִימְּצָהּ וְיָצָאת, וְחָזַר וְחִימְּצָהּ – מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the exemption for a disqualified מנחה from step 14 to a case where it became disqualified only after the first leavening.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is one liable for leavening a מנחה a second time after it became פסול יוצא, when the first leavening was done while it was fit?

steps.title: First side: going out disqualifies it, so no liability
steps.stepSummary: Maybe once it left the עזרה it became פסולה through יוצא. Then the second leavening is on a disqualified מנחה, and he is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it went out, it became disqualified as something that left its place. So when he leavens it again, he is not liable for leavening it after it was already leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first side of רב פפא's question: why the second leavening might not be punishable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, leavening a מנחה that someone already leavened is still punishable. But by this side, leaving the עזרה turned it into a פסולה. Step 14 taught that a disqualified מנחה is not covered, so the second leavening is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
It became disqualified
Something holy that left its allowed area, which disqualifies it
Leavening after someone already leavened it

phrases.english: Since it went out,
it became disqualified as something that went out,
and when he leavens it again,
he is not liable for it
for leavening after one who already leavened.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּיָצָאת אִיפְּסִילָה לַהּ בְּיוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first possible answer to רב פפא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: First side: does the disqualification of יוצא take effect and exempt the second leavening?

steps.title: Second side: going out changes nothing, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe, since it was already leavened, the disqualification of יוצא does not take hold on it. Then the second leavening is punishable like any leavening after leavening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, since it was already leavened, the disqualification of going out has no effect on it. So when he leavens it again, he is liable for leavening it after it was already leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: the going-out might not change the מנחה's status at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this side, the first leavening already set the מנחה's status. The later going-out adds no new disqualification that matters here. So the מנחה is treated as before, and the normal rule applies: leavening after leavening is punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Has no effect, does not take hold
The disqualification caused by leaving the allowed area

phrases.english: Or perhaps, since he already leavened it,
the disqualification of going out has no effect on it,
and when he leavens it again,
he is liable for it
for leavening after one who already leavened?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּחִימְּצָהּ, פְּסוּל יוֹצֵא לָא מַהֲנֵי בַּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite possibility to step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Second side: does the earlier leavening block the יוצא disqualification, so the second leavening is still punishable?

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds no answer, and רב פפא's question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand — the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב פפא's question without deciding between the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side is proven. So we do not know whether the second leavening, after the מנחה left the עזרה, is punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: A fit מנחה may not be made חמץ; a disqualified one is exempt. Whether leaving the עזרה after a first leavening exempts a second leavening stays an open question (תיקו).
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'not liable' or 'liable'. It means the גמרא never decided.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רב פפא's question with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of liability for leavening again after the מנחה became פסול יוצא remains unresolved.

steps.title: Leavening a מנחה at the top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי asks about a מנחה that was leavened after it was already brought up to the top of the מזבח. Is the person liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי asked: if someone leavened a מנחה at the top of the מזבח, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב מרי asks whether leavening a מנחה is still forbidden once the מנחה is already up on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב פפא before him, רב מרי is looking for the edge of the חימוץ prohibition. Here the issue is timing: the מנחה has reached the מזבח but has not yet been burned. The next two steps lay out the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he was unsure about)
He leavened it (made it חמץ)
The top of the altar

phrases.english: Rav Mari asked:
If he leavened it at the top of the altar,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's question was left unresolved, a second question about the limits of the חימוץ prohibition is raised.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the חימוץ prohibition apply to a מנחה that is already on top of the מזבח but not yet burned?

steps.title: First side: it was already brought
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'אשר תקריבו', meaning 'that you will bring'. This מנחה has already been brought, so maybe the prohibition no longer applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah said 'that you shall bring', and this one has already been brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first side of רב מרי's question. Maybe there is no liability, because the מנחה has already been brought up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'אשר תקריבו' points to a מנחה that is still going to be brought. Once it is on the מזבח, it has already been 'brought', so it may fall outside the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That you shall bring': the words in the פסוק about the חימוץ prohibition
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
He has brought it (it was already offered up)

phrases.english: "That you shall bring," said the Merciful One,
and this one he has already brought.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשֶׁר תַּקְרִיבוּ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא וְהָא אַקְרְבַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the first possible answer to the question in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'אשר תקריבו' exclude a מנחה that has already reached the מזבח?

steps.title: Second side: it still needs burning
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe a מנחה that has not yet been burned counts as one whose service is not finished, so it is still covered by the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps something that still lacks burning is considered like something that still lacks its action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side. Maybe the person is liable, because the מנחה has not yet been burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key act for a מנחה is the הקטרה (burning on the fire). If that has not happened yet, the מנחה may still count as 'not yet brought', even though it is physically on the מזבח. If so, the prohibition still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Still lacking burning on the altar
Still lacking an action (its service is not complete)

phrases.english: Or perhaps
something that still lacks burning
is considered like something that still lacks an action?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא מְחוּסַּר הַקְטָרָה כִּמְחוּסַּר מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite possibility to step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a מנחה that has not yet been burned treated as not yet 'brought'?

steps.title: Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, and רב מרי's question stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two sides, so the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like רב פפא's question, this question ends in תיקו. We do not know whether leavening a מנחה on top of the מזבח makes a person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: Both questions about the limits of the חימוץ prohibition are left unresolved: רב פפא's question about יוצא and רב מרי's question about leavening on top of the מזבח.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question opened in step 19 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether leavening a מנחה at the top of the מזבח is punishable remains a תיקו.

steps.title: Why do we need 'אשר תקריבו'?
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition is already learned from 'כל המנחה'. So what extra lesson do the words 'אשר תקריבו' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that he derives it from 'any meal offering', why do I need 'that you shall bring (to ה׳)'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the verse and asks why it needs the extra words 'אשר תקריבו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's teacher already learned from 'כל המנחה' that the prohibition covers a מנחה even before its קמיצה. The Torah does not use extra words for nothing. So the words 'אשר תקריבו' must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And now (that we have established this)
He derives it (from a verse)
'Any meal offering': the opening words of the פסוק
Why do I need it? (asks for the purpose of seemingly extra words)

phrases.english: And now that he derives it
from "any meal offering,"
why do I need "that you shall bring (to ה׳)"?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The question is really about 'אשר תקריבו'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִכׇּל הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the unresolved questions and returns to how the words of the verse are used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'אשר תקריבו' in the ברייתא's derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'כל המנחה' already covers the prohibition, so the words 'אשר תקריבו' look extra and need their own purpose.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: to include מנחת נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The words are needed for a ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי says they add מנחת נסכים to the חימוץ prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught: 'That you shall bring' comes to include the libation meal offering in the leavening prohibition. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'אשר תקריבו' teaches a separate lesson. It quotes a ברייתא, starting with רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחת נסכים is the flour offering that comes along with certain animal קרבנות. It is not a regular מנחה from which a קמיצה is taken; it is burned completely. So a separate source is needed to include it in the חימוץ prohibition, and 'אשר תקריבו' provides it.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for another lesson)
To include (to add a case to the law)
The flour offering that comes with the libations of certain animal offerings
Leavening (making it חמץ)

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught:
"That you shall bring" —
comes to include the libation meal offering in the leavening prohibition,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by giving the extra words a purpose of their own.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the seemingly extra words a separate lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשר תקריבו' seemed to add nothing beyond 'כל המנחה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אשר תקריבו' adds מנחת נסכים to the חימוץ prohibition (according to רבי יוסי הגלילי).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: to include לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. He says 'אשר תקריבו' adds לחם הפנים to the חימוץ prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: it comes to include the showbread in the leavening prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion. רבי עקיבא reads the same words as adding לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that 'אשר תקריבו' adds something to the prohibition. They disagree about what it adds. For רבי יוסי הגלילי it is מנחת נסכים; for רבי עקיבא it is לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread placed on the שולחן in the משכן and מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
it comes to include the showbread in the leavening prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לְרַבּוֹת לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים לְחִימּוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the same words, in disagreement with רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, 'אשר תקריבו' brings לחם הפנים under the חימוץ prohibition.

steps.title: Can מנחת נסכים become חמץ at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רבי יוסי הגלילי. מנחת נסכים is mixed with oil, which counts as fruit juice. So how could it become חמץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: The libation meal offering? It is fruit juice!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts questioning רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחת נסכים is mixed with olive oil, not water, and oil counts as fruit juice. The point of the challenge is that dough made with fruit juice does not truly become חמץ. If so, why would the Torah need to forbid leavening it?

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit juice (any liquid from fruit, including olive oil)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מי פירות' does not mean the offering is a drink. It means the dough is mixed with oil, which counts in הלכה as fruit juice rather than water.

phrases.english: The libation meal offering?
It is fruit juice!
phrases.notes: He means the oil it is kneaded with counts as fruit juice, not water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת נְסָכִים מֵי פֵירוֹת הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that 'אשר תקריבו' includes מנחת נסכים in the חימוץ prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחת נסכים is made with oil, which counts as fruit juice. Fruit juice does not make dough truly חמץ, so a prohibition against leavening it seems pointless.
